How to use Font Maker

The guide lines

Every letter sits inside five horizontal lines. From bottom to top:

  • Descender — the lowest line. Only the tails of g j p q y reach down this far.
  • Baseline — the main writing line, like the ruled line in a notebook. Almost every letter's bottom sits right on it.
  • x-height — the top of lowercase letters with no tall stem, like a c e m n o.
  • Cap height — the top of capital letters (A B C…).
  • Ascender — the highest line. Tall lowercase letters like b d h k l t reach up this far.

On the canvas, the line that matters for whichever letter you're drawing is drawn bold blue — x-height for lowercase, cap height for capitals — so it's always clear where that letter should top out. The baseline is always the darkest black line.

These five lines only describe one letter's own height, not the gap between lines of text — that spacing is set separately, later, by whatever uses this font (a document, a text box, and so on), so the ascender of this letter never "collides" with anything here.

The two vertical blue lines are different: they mark this one character's own width — start on the left, and advance on the right, which is where the next letter will begin. They control side-to-side spacing, not height.

Moving the lines. Each line has a small tab at its right end showing its number. Drag a tab to move Ascender, Cap height, x-height or Descender; drag the tab at the top of the advance line to change this letter's width. Double-tap a tab to put its line back. The height lines apply to the whole font and are saved with it, and the letter guides on the vector screen follow them. Baseline and start stay fixed because everything is measured from them.

Draw a letter

  • Pick a letter from the strip at the top. Use the 0–9 / ! ? . tabs to switch sets, and Aa ⇄ to switch between uppercase and lowercase (or jump to this letter's other case).
  • To draw or reshape a letter directly against its guide lines, tap 〰️ Curves to leave Font Maker, then hold the ▦ Grid button and tap Letter guides. Switch back to Font Maker when you're done to pick the next one.
  • Once it's drawn, select it on the Curves canvas, then come back here and hold your finger on this letter to Paste it in.

Bring in vector art

On the drawing canvas, select your polished shapes, lines or text and tap Copy (or just leave them selected). Then here hold your finger down on the letter and tap 📥 Paste — it drops straight onto the letter, sized and centered automatically.

  • Not quite right? Tap the shape on the canvas to pick it back up. Drag it to move, drag the square handles to resize.
  • 🔒 Ratio keeps proportions. Shift flips it.
  • Cap / x-ht / Asc / Desc fit it to the guide lines.
  • Tap anywhere outside the box to drop it back in when you're happy, or tap 🗑️ Delete to remove it.
  • Lines and outlines become real filled outlines, and overlapping pieces are merged. Use Subtract on the canvas to make holes.

Snap, scale and copy

  • Snap pulls a shape you've picked back up to the guide lines, the letter edges, and an optional Grid. Pink lines show what it caught.
  • With the Select tool, tap any shape's body (not a point) to lift it and resize/move it with the same handles.
  • Hold your finger down on a letter to Copy or Paste its shape (or use Ctrl/Cmd+C and V) — reuses a shape from one letter on another.

Copying a whole style

  • Hold down on the style button (⇄) to copy every letter of the style you're currently drawing.
  • Switch to a different style, then hold the button again to paste — hold once more to confirm, since this replaces that style's letters.

Bold & Italic

Every style is its own set of letters, spacing and kerning that you make yourself. Tap a chip at the top to draw that style, tap its 📂 to attach a font file (the .json from Save Font) instead, or tap its 🗑️ to clear it. Save a finished style as its own file further down in the menu. The Text tool’s B and I buttons then use these letters.

Kerning

Kerning fine-tunes the space between a specific pair of letters (for example “A” + “V”). Choose the pair, then type a value and tap Set, or use the −50 / −10 / +10 / +50 buttons.

  • Drag the picture left or right to move the second letter closer or further away.
  • The green band is the white space between the two letters (the bold bar marks the tightest spot). It turns red where they touch.
  • Blue and orange boxes are each letter’s advance width. The dashed blue outline shows where the second letter sat before kerning.
  • Changes save as you go. Tap a pair in the list to load it.

Saving your font

This font belongs to the current document: a new document starts with a blank font, and Save Project keeps the font inside the project file.

Save Font stores just the font as its own file, so you can pick up where you left off or reuse it in another document.
